worlds_section.label: The Deck's Mythology
worlds_section.title: 4 worlds in 54 paintings
worlds_section.lead: Magister is a unique custom 54-card deck, based on the classic four-suit system that incorporates symbols from Ancient mythology, the Middle Ages, and modern culture.
worlds_section.mechanic: Images and scenes on each card encode its suit and rank. But as the suits and ranks aren't marked on the cards, they all must be determined using the following symbol system.

hearts.name: Olympic Gods
hearts.blurb: The classical pantheon in motion: desire, metamorphosis, oracle and flame. Hearts carry mythic episodes where mortals and immortals negotiate fate.

diamonds.name: Bearers of Secrets
diamonds.blurb: Alchemical emissaries, hidden orders, and whispers behind crowns. Diamonds track those who traffic in knowledge that should not travel in plain sight.

clubs.name: Templars
clubs.blurb: Crusade steel, lost treasure-maps, and the long shadow of the order. Clubs anchor the deck in medieval intrigue and the arc from devotion to legend.

spades.name: Celebrities
spades.blurb: Modern myth-making: faces the world thought it knew, reframed as archetypes. Spades ask what happens when public masks become permanent emblems.

authors.preface_p1: Long before Magister became a deck of cards, there were paintings.
authors.preface_p2: Vasily Pochitsky and Alexander Zhilchik spent years creating their own worlds — inventing characters, places and stories, and bringing them to life on canvas.
authors.preface_p3: Each of the 54 cards is based on one of these original works.
authors.preface_p4: The deck is only a glimpse into a much larger world.
authors.preface_image_alt: Original Magister paintings on the studio wall; Alexander Zhilchik and Vasily Pochitsky with the card deck.
authors.label: Authors
authors.title: Authors of Magister Cards

pochitsky.name: Vasily Pochitsky
pochitsky.role: Artist and co-creator of the Magister universe.
pochitsky.bio: Belarusian painter, illustrator and musician. He began painting in Rechitsa and went on to exhibit from Moscow to New York. For nearly a decade, his drawings appeared in the national press, and throughout his career he illustrated books and records.
pochitsky.bio_2: Magister was his most ambitious cycle: created in close collaboration with Alexander Zhilchik, the fifty-four paintings brought their shared world and its characters to life on canvas.

zhilchik.name: Alexander Zhilchik
zhilchik.bio: Zhilchik developed the mythology behind the cycle — its houses, characters, relationships and historical threads.
zhilchik.bio_2: Together with Vasily Pochitsky, he imagined and developed the world that would eventually take shape across the paintings.
